purpose: How a merchant-processing/POS agent turns a signed merchant into a live, correctly configured, trained and settling card-acceptance operation - matching POS hardware and software to the vertical, shepherding an honest application through the processor's underwriting and KYC path, executing site survey, menu build, installation, legacy cutover and staff training, containing PCI scope at deployment, and running go-live hypercare through verified first settlement into a clean handoff to portfolio management.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all scores are heuristic priors
the agent operates under an ISO/agent program with a sponsoring processor already selected; program choice and agreement terms belong to the sibling acquisition KB
interchange, markup, equipment pricing and residual splits appear only as mechanisms or qualitative bands - no specific rate, price or percentage is asserted as fact

card-network rules, PCI-DSS requirements and surcharging law are jurisdiction-, network- and version-specific compliance classes; current rules must be verified before any configuration that depends on them
the underwriting decision belongs to the sponsoring processor; the agent prepares and shepherds an honest application file and never guarantees approval
target merchants are small-format brick-and-mortar operators - restaurants, salons, convenience stores, auto shops - typical of an agent's local book
exclusions: ISO/agent program selection, agent-agreement terms, vertical targeting strategy, the bundle-led sales relationship (POS plus phones, internet, cameras, support), statement analysis and sales-claim compliance - the merchant-acquisition sibling KB owns all of it

residual stream computation and payment mechanics, attrition and merchant-level margin health, long-run support economics, chargeback education for merchants, cross-sell plays and portfolio valuation or sale - the residual-book sibling KB owns all of it
invented rates, savings percentages, equipment prices or split figures stated as fact - processing economics are described only as mechanisms with a per-merchant verification path
rendering underwriting verdicts - approving, declining, pricing or reserving against a merchant is the processor's decision; this KB covers only preparing and reacting to that process honestly

legal, tax or financial advice on merchant contracts, entity structure, surcharge legality or fee disputes, and QSA-grade PCI assessment services - deployment work names the compliance class and routes to qualified professionals
deceptive onboarding of any kind: coached misstatements on applications, undisclosed lease terms, savings claims restated at install without per-merchant verification

competency_questions.question: Which POS platform and hardware package fits a given merchant vertical's daily workflow, and what evidence proves the fit before anything is ordered?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: VERTICAL_FIT_PROFILE names the workflow facts to capture per vertical (restaurant, salon, c-store, auto shop) and HARDWARE_SOFTWARE_SELECTION shows how those facts select terminal class, peripherals and software capabilities

competency_questions.question: What must a merchant application packet contain before submission, and why does packet quality set the speed of everything downstream?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MERCHANT_INTAKE_PACKET lists the document set (legal entity, taxpayer ID, ownership, banking proof, processing history) and the consistency checks that prevent underwriting pends

competency_questions.question: What does the processor's underwriting and KYC path actually verify, and where does the agent's role end and the processor's decision begin?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: UNDERWRITING_PATH walks the verification stages (identity, ownership, MATCH screen, credit, business legitimacy, volume plausibility) and states that the verdict belongs to the processor; MCC_AND_RISK_CLASS explains how classification feeds the review

competency_questions.question: What most often delays or kills a merchant application, and what is the honest triage move for each cause?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: UNDERWRITING_DELAY_KILLERS enumerates the recurring stall and kill causes (name and bank mismatches, missing signatures, prohibited lines of business, prior MATCH placement, implausible volumes) each with a repair-or-route response that never coaches misstatement

competency_questions.question: When should existing equipment be reprogrammed instead of replaced, and how are sale, lease and placement structures disclosed honestly?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: HARDWARE_SOFTWARE_SELECTION gives the reprogram-versus-replace decision test and describes sale, lease and placement as cost-structure mechanisms; ETHICAL_ONBOARDING_RULES requires plain-language disclosure of term, total obligation and cancellation before signature

competency_questions.question: What must a pre-install site survey establish about power, network and counter reality before an install date is fixed?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SITE_SURVEY_READINESS lists the survey checks (internet reliability and failover, drops and Wi-Fi coverage, power at stations, counter space, cable paths, busy-hours windows) and NETWORK_SEGMENTATION_BASICS states the segmentation work the survey must scope

competency_questions.question: How is the menu or catalog built, tax-mapped and verified so day-one orders ring correctly?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MENU_CATALOG_BUILD covers source-data gathering, modifier and variant structure, tax category mapping, the owner proof pass, and the menu freeze that protects the build

competency_questions.question: How is the cutover from the legacy processor and POS planned so card acceptance never gaps and gift-card liability survives the switch?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LEGACY_CUTOVER_PLAN sequences last-batch and first-live-transaction timing, gift-card and card-on-file data handling, equipment-return obligations and honest surfacing of the old contract's termination terms

competency_questions.question: What determines a merchant's PCI scope at deployment, and which install-time choices shrink it?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PCI_SCOPE_AT_DEPLOYMENT explains scope as a function of how card data flows (validated P2PE, segmentation, no manual card-data handling) and flags SAQ typing as version-specific to verify; NETWORK_SEGMENTATION_BASICS supplies the concrete network hygiene

competency_questions.question: Under what conditions may tip prompts, surcharging or cash discounting be configured at deployment, and what must be verified first?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TIP_AND_SURCHARGE_CONFIG distinguishes tip capture modes by service environment and treats surcharge and cash-discount programs as jurisdiction- and network-rule-governed classes that require verification and correct receipt disclosure before enablement

competency_questions.question: What does role-based staff training cover for each vertical, and how does it survive staff turnover?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: STAFF_TRAINING separates cashier/server flows from manager flows (voids, refunds, comps, end-of-day, reports), covers tip and offline behavior, and leaves durable artifacts - quick-reference cards and a train-the-trainer path

competency_questions.question: What does go-live hypercare watch in the first days of live processing, and what gets fixed on the spot?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: GO_LIVE_SUPPORT defines the hypercare window, the on-site day-one presence, the first end-of-day close walkthrough, the rapid-fix loop for menu and tax errors, and the escalation split between agent, platform and processor support

competency_questions.question: How is the first settlement verified from batch to bank deposit, and what does a missing or short deposit indicate?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FIRST_SETTLEMENT_VERIFICATION traces batch close to funding arrival, names the classic failure causes (miskeyed bank account, held funds, descriptor confusion, tip-adjust variance) and the correction path with the processor

competency_questions.question: When is a deployment done, and how are several deployments run in parallel without starving any single merchant's go-live?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: HANDOFF_TO_PORTFOLIO states the definition-of-done (live, settled, trained, documented, PCI attestation underway) enforced through DEPLOYMENT_RECORD_HANDOFF, while DEPLOYMENT_SCHEDULING_PIPELINE and DEPLOYMENT_SCOPE_FRAME bound how much parallel work the calendar may carry

glossary.definition: The four-digit code that classifies a merchant's line of business at boarding; it feeds interchange qualification classes, risk screening and ongoing monitoring thresholds, so a wrong MCC set at deployment resurfaces later as holds, downgrades or a forced re-board.

The identity-verification class a processor must run on the business and its controlling owners (commonly those at or above a control-percentage threshold defined by current rules); mismatched legal names, addresses or taxpayer IDs between documents are the classic cause of a stalled file.

The card-brand-operated database of terminated merchants that processors screen during underwriting; a prior placement follows the principal, not just the old business name, and the honest response is disclosure and routing to processors that handle that history - never concealment behind a new entity.

The card-network-published per-transaction fee mechanism paid toward the issuing bank; deployment never quotes it as a number, but install-time facts - correct MCC, card-present entry modes, timely batching - determine which interchange classes the merchant's transactions qualify for.

An encryption approach where card data is encrypted inside the reader and decrypted only by the solution provider, so the merchant's POS, network and staff never touch usable card data; a validated P2PE listing is the strongest deployment-time lever for shrinking PCI scope.

The PCI-DSS instrument a small merchant completes to attest compliance; which SAQ class applies depends on how the deployed stack handles card data, and the class definitions move with PCI-DSS versions - verify the current version rather than reciting a remembered type.

The end-of-day close that submits the day's captured transactions for clearing and funding; the deposit that lands is the batch total transformed by the pricing mechanism and any holds, so tracing batch-to-deposit is how deployment configuration errors are caught early.

The planned seam between the legacy stack and the new one: the last batch on the old processor, the first live transaction on the new POS, and the managed migration of everything that must cross the seam - gift-card liability, card-on-file expectations, equipment-return obligations.

Two distinct price-signaling programs: a surcharge adds a disclosed fee to card payments, a cash discount reduces a posted price for cash; whether each is permitted, how it is capped, registered and shown on receipts is governed by jurisdiction law and card-network rules that must be verified before the feature is switched on.

The deliberately over-staffed support window from first live transaction through verified first settlement, when configuration errors are cheapest to fix, staff habits are still forming and the merchant's trust in the whole relationship is won or lost.

nodes.definition: Fix what deployment-and-onboarding owns: everything from a signed merchant agreement to a stabilized live operation, with an explicit definition-of-done - the merchant is accepting cards correctly on equipment matched to their workflow, staff can run a full day unaided, first settlement has been verified against the batch, the deployment record exists, and the PCI attestation path has been started. The frame also draws the two borders this work must not cross: selling and program economics live upstream in acquisition, and residual, retention and cross-sell live downstream in portfolio management. Holding this frame stops deployment from becoming an open-ended support engagement or a second sales call.

included: borders with acquisition and portfolio work

pros.claim: A written done-definition keeps every deployment converging on the same finish line instead of drifting per merchant
pros.example: a taqueria install closes when the owner has run three unaided closes and the first deposit reconciled - not when the owner stops calling

cons.claim: A rigid frame can make the agent ignore live problems that straddle the border into portfolio territory
cons.example: declaring done while a simmering tip-pooling dispute is about to become week-two churn

failure_modes: deployment scope creeps into unpaid general IT support and never closes
declaring done on installed hardware alone, before settlement and training are proven
acceptance_tests: the frame document states the entry event, the done-definition items, and the named boundaries with the acquisition and portfolio phases
revisit_triggers: a new vertical or product bundle changes what a finished deployment must include
repeated handoff bounce-backs show the done-definition is too weak

base.update_signal: the program's deliverables or the sibling-KB boundaries are restated

nodes.definition: Bind every onboarding step to disclosure-first conduct: equipment sale, lease or placement terms are explained in plain language - term length, total obligation over the term, cancellation and return conditions - before any signature; no savings figure from the sales conversation is restated at install unless it was verified against that merchant's own statements; application facts are the merchant's true facts, never coached; and extra care applies to vulnerable operators - first-time owners, merchants working through a language barrier, family businesses signing under pressure - who get slower walkthroughs and written summaries rather than faster closes. These rules are identity, not garnish: a book built on clean onboarding survives; one built on buried terms attrits and invites disputes.

pros.claim: Disclosure-first onboarding removes the ambush moments that create cancellations and chargebacks against the agent's reputation
pros.example: a salon owner who saw the lease's full-term obligation on paper before signing does not rage-cancel in month three when a competitor waves a cheaper flyer

cons.claim: Full disclosure slows the close and occasionally loses a deal a pushier competitor wins
cons.example: a c-store owner postpones after seeing the lease's total cost written out - and a rival signs them that week on an unread contract

failure_modes: an unverified savings promise from the sales call is repeated at install and becomes the merchant's expectation
lease paperwork is signed on a screen the merchant never scrolled
acceptance_tests: every signed equipment agreement has a dated plain-language summary the merchant received before signature, and no application field was completed by the agent on the merchant's behalf without the merchant confirming the fact
revisit_triggers: a merchant dispute or regulator inquiry cites an onboarding disclosure gap
the program adds a new financing or leasing product whose terms need a new summary format

base.update_signal: a dispute, clawback or complaint traces to an onboarding conduct gap

nodes.definition: Assemble the application packet that underwriting will actually read: legal entity name exactly as registered, taxpayer ID, ownership breakdown down to the control threshold current rules define, government ID for each principal, a banking proof (voided check or bank letter) whose account name matches the legal or DBA name, physical and mailing addresses, prior processing history if any, and the signed program paperwork. The craft is consistency-checking before submission - DBA versus legal name, address across documents, signer authority versus ownership - because underwriting queues punish mismatches with pends measured in days. A clean packet is the single highest-leverage speed input the agent controls.

pros.claim: Pre-submission consistency checks convert multi-day underwriting pends into same-queue approvals
pros.example: catching that the mechanic's bank letter says the owner's personal name while the application says the LLC - fixed with one bank visit before submission instead of a week-long pend after

cons.claim: An exhaustive intake ritual frustrates simple merchants and can stall momentum on easy files
cons.example: a single-owner barbershop asked for documents twice because the checklist was applied bureaucratically rather than fitted to the entity type

failure_modes: submitting with a DBA/legal-name mismatch that pends the file and later mis-routes funding
missing beneficial-owner details for a multi-member LLC, triggering a KYC information request cycle
acceptance_tests: before submission, the packet passes a written consistency check: entity name, taxpayer ID, ownership to threshold, matching banking proof, valid IDs, and all signatures present
revisit_triggers: the processor changes its required-document list or ownership threshold
a pend-reason log shows a recurring missing item the checklist does not catch

base.update_signal: processor document requirements change or pend reasons shift

nodes.definition: Capture the workflow facts that determine what the POS must actually do for this merchant's vertical before any product is proposed: a table-service restaurant needs coursing, seat-level ordering, tip adjust, kitchen routing and split checks; a quick-service counter needs speed, modifiers and kitchen display throughput; a salon needs appointments, service providers, booth-renter separation and card-on-file expectations; a c-store needs scan speed, PLU/UPC price-book scale, age-verification prompts and possibly EBT and lottery workflows; an auto shop needs estimates, invoices, partial payments and card-on-file authorizations. The profile is written from observation and owner interview - watching a lunch rush teaches more than any brochure - and it becomes the requirements sheet every later choice is tested against.

included: the requirements sheet as fit test
excluded: choosing which verticals to target - acquisition territory

pros.claim: A written workflow profile prevents the classic mis-sale of a retail-style POS into a service business
pros.example: discovering the salon's booth renters each need their own payouts before proposing a single-drawer retail setup that would have died in week one

cons.claim: Deep profiling takes owner time and can feel like a delay to a merchant who just wants the box installed
cons.example: a c-store owner irritated by an hour of price-book questions when the old register 'worked fine'

failure_modes: profiling from the owner's summary alone and missing how the floor actually runs during rush
copying the last restaurant's profile onto a different service model
acceptance_tests: the profile names the vertical's non-negotiable workflows, the observed peak-hour realities, and the features the current system lacks or provides
revisit_triggers: the merchant changes service model - adds delivery, a food truck, online ordering, booth renters
go-live reveals a workflow the profile missed

base.update_signal: the merchant's service model or peak-hour workflow changes

nodes.definition: Translate the vertical profile into a concrete stack decision on two axes. Axis one is capability class: reprogram the merchant's existing compliant terminal, place a smart terminal, or deploy a full POS with stations, handhelds and peripherals (cash drawer, receipt and kitchen printers, kitchen display, barcode scanner, scale where the vertical needs it) - chosen by workflow need, not by what pays the agent most. Axis two is acquisition structure as a mechanism: outright sale front-loads cost and ends there; a lease spreads payments but its total-term obligation usually exceeds the hardware's price several times over and survives merchant remorse; free placement embeds the cost in processing economics and binds the relationship. The node's discipline is right-sizing: the smallest stack that runs the merchant's day well, with the structure the merchant understood on paper.

excluded: quoting specific prices or lease rates as market fact
the processing-economics share design - acquisition territory

pros.claim: Right-sizing the stack to the profile produces installs that stick instead of getting ripped out by the next agent
pros.example: reprogramming a mechanic's working terminal and adding invoicing software beats forcing a three-station POS the shop never needed

cons.claim: The equipment decision carries the agent's own revenue conflict, which right-sizing rules constrain but cannot delete
cons.example: a lease commission tempting an oversized bundle into a two-chair barbershop

failure_modes: selecting the platform the agent knows instead of the platform the vertical needs
placing leased equipment whose total obligation the merchant never saw written out
acceptance_tests: the selected stack maps every non-negotiable workflow in the profile to a demonstrated feature, and the acquisition structure's full term and total obligation appear in the merchant's plain-language summary
revisit_triggers: the platform vendor changes hardware compatibility, certification or feature support
go-live or training exposes a workflow the selected stack cannot run

base.update_signal: platform certifications, hardware lines or program equipment options change

nodes.definition: Get the merchant classified truthfully at boarding: the MCC that genuinely matches the line of business, monthly volume and average-ticket estimates drawn from real history or a defensible projection, and card-present versus keyed mix stated as the business actually runs. These fields are not paperwork trivia - they calibrate the processor's fraud monitoring, so an understated volume estimate triggers a funding hold the first busy weekend, and a convenience MCC chosen to dodge scrutiny is a misrepresentation that surfaces at the worst time. Certain lines of business fall into prohibited or registration-required classes under processor policy and network rules; the agent's job is recognizing the class early and routing honestly, not disguising the business.

included: volume and ticket profiling from evidence
excluded: the processor's risk decision and pricing
asserting which categories any given processor accepts - verify per program

pros.claim: Honest volume and ticket profiling prevents the week-one funding hold that destroys a new merchant's trust
pros.example: profiling the c-store's lottery-season weekend spikes into the application so the first big Saturday does not trip a velocity review

cons.claim: Accurate classification sometimes prices or screens a merchant worse than a looser one would have, testing the agent's honesty
cons.example: a shop whose real mix includes a high keyed-entry share underwrites less favorably than if the agent had shaded the mix

failure_modes: lowballing projected volume to ease approval, guaranteeing a later hold
misclassifying a business into a friendlier MCC and creating a misrepresentation discovered at audit
acceptance_tests: the MCC, volume, ticket and entry-mode fields each trace to a stated evidence source - prior statements, comparable-store reasoning, or the owner's documented estimate
revisit_triggers: the merchant's real volume or mix diverges materially from the boarded profile
network or processor category rules change for this line of business

base.update_signal: boarded profile diverges from observed processing or category rules change

nodes.definition: Know the processor's verification path well enough to shepherd a file through it without ever owning the verdict: identity and beneficial-ownership checks against the submitted IDs, MATCH-list screening of the business and principals, a credit review of the business and often the signing owner, business-legitimacy checks (site, web presence, license where applicable, consistency between claimed line of business and observable reality), and plausibility review of the volume profile. The agent's levers are preparation and response speed - submitting clean, answering information requests same-day, and setting the merchant's expectation that underwriting is the processor's gate with its own clock. The verdict - approve, approve with conditions such as reserves or volume caps, or decline - belongs to the processor, and repeating that boundary to the merchant is part of the job.

included: the verification stages as a path to prepare for
same-day response discipline on information requests
excluded: advising on credit repair or legal structuring

pros.claim: Knowing the stages lets the agent pre-answer the questions underwriting will ask, collapsing cycle time
pros.example: attaching the new restaurant's lease and health permit up front because legitimacy review always asks a brand-new entity for them

cons.claim: A shepherded file can still stall on the processor's internal queue, and the agent absorbs merchant frustration for a clock they do not control
cons.example: a spotless salon application sitting in a backlog while the owner's launch date slips

failure_modes: promising approval or a live date before the verdict exists
letting an information request age a week because nobody watched the queue
acceptance_tests: every submitted file has a status log showing submission date, each information request and its same-day-or-next response, and the communicated expectation that the processor decides
revisit_triggers: the processor changes its underwriting stages, thresholds or document demands
conditional approvals (reserves, caps) start appearing on a merchant type that used to board clean

base.update_signal: processor underwriting stages, conditions or timelines change

nodes.definition: Maintain the triage playbook for what actually stalls or kills files, with an honest response per cause. Stalls: name or banking mismatches (fix the document, resubmit), missing signer or beneficial-owner data (collect and refile), unverifiable business address or absent web footprint for a delivery-dependent claim (supply lease, photos, license), stale or missing financials on larger volume requests. Kills: prohibited line of business under the program (route to a program that accepts the class, or decline the deal), prior MATCH placement (disclose, explain, route to specialist processors - never re-mask the principal behind a fresh entity), fabricated volume history (walk away). The playbook's spine is a pend-reason log across all files, because recurring reasons are intake defects to fix upstream, not fate.

included: the pend-reason log as an improvement loop
excluded: appealing the processor's judgment beyond supplying facts

pros.claim: A cause-by-cause playbook turns pends from dead time into a one-cycle repair
pros.example: a bank-letter mismatch caught and fixed the same afternoon because the playbook names exactly which document cures it

cons.claim: Triage energy spent on a fundamentally unbankable file is wasted acquisition cost
cons.example: three repair cycles on a merchant whose real problem is an undisclosed MATCH placement that surfaces at the end anyway

failure_modes: treating every pend as processor slowness instead of reading the stated reason
helping a declined merchant re-apply under a spouse's name - a program-terminating offense
acceptance_tests: each pended or declined file shows the stated reason, the response taken, and the log entry that feeds the intake checklist
revisit_triggers: a new pend reason appears that the playbook lacks
the pend-reason log shows one cause recurring across files

base.update_signal: a new stall or kill cause appears or an old cause changes its cure

nodes.definition: Walk the site before hardware is ordered or an install date is promised, and record what the room actually offers: internet service type and observed reliability, router and switch port availability, Wi-Fi coverage at every point a handheld or terminal will live, power outlets at each station and at the kitchen printer location, counter depth and mounting reality, cable paths that do not cross a fry station, cellular signal for an LTE failover, and the merchant's real busy hours so the install lands in the quiet window. The survey converts the install from an improvisation into a checklist and produces the remediation list - a new drop, a switch, a conduit run - that must finish before install day.

included: network, power, space and signal audit
the remediation list as an install gate
excluded: performing electrician-grade or ISP work - subcontract it

pros.claim: A surveyed site turns install day into execution instead of discovery
pros.example: learning on the walk-through that the c-store's back office has the only router and it sits on the public counter circuit - fixed with a scheduled electrician, not on install morning

cons.claim: A survey visit adds a trip and days of lead time that a simple single-terminal swap may not need
cons.example: a countertop reprogram for a barbershop delayed a week by survey scheduling that a photo exchange could have replaced

failure_modes: ordering hardware before the survey and discovering the counter cannot hold the chosen station
assuming the merchant's 'good Wi-Fi' claim and losing handheld ordering in the patio dead zone
acceptance_tests: the survey record covers connectivity, power, space, signal and install window, and every remediation item has an owner and a due date before the install date
revisit_triggers: the merchant remodels, moves or changes ISP before install
an install-day surprise reveals a check the survey template lacks

base.update_signal: site conditions change or install-day surprises expose survey gaps

nodes.definition: Build the data layer the merchant will ring against: for a restaurant, the full menu with modifier groups, coursing, sizes and kitchen-routing assignments; for a salon, the service list with durations, providers and retail add-ons; for a c-store, the department structure and the PLU/UPC price book at scale; for an auto shop, labor and parts line items with taxable/non-taxable splits. Two disciplines make or break it: tax-category mapping done against the jurisdiction's actual rules (prepared food versus grocery, service versus retail - verify locally, never guess), and a menu freeze - a declared date after which owner changes queue into a post-live change log instead of endlessly reopening the build. The build ends with a proof pass where the owner rings realistic orders and signs off item names, prices, modifiers and tax lines.

included: item, modifier and routing structure per vertical
menu freeze and owner proof pass
excluded: tax advice beyond flagging classes to verify
ongoing post-live menu management as a service line

pros.claim: An owner-signed proof pass catches the errors that would otherwise become day-one line-stalls and wrong tickets
pros.example: the proof pass catches that combo modifiers double-charge the drink and that prepared-food tax is on the packaged sodas

cons.claim: A large or volatile catalog makes the build the schedule's long pole and a cost sink on small deals
cons.example: a c-store's multi-thousand-item price book arriving as a shoebox of shelf tags

failure_modes: building from an out-of-date menu photo while the owner keeps changing prices verbally
guessing tax categories and creating a compliance and refund mess discovered weeks after live
acceptance_tests: the owner proof pass is signed against realistic rung orders, tax mapping carries a verify-locally note per ambiguous class, and the freeze date with its post-live change log is in force
revisit_triggers: the merchant changes menu, services or pricing structure before go-live
a tax-rule change or an audit question hits a mapped category

base.update_signal: menu volatility, tax-rule changes or proof-pass defect patterns

nodes.definition: Plan the seam between the old stack and the new one so the merchant never stops accepting cards and no liability is orphaned. The plan times the last settled batch on the legacy processor against the first live transaction on the new stack; inventories what must cross the seam - outstanding gift-card balances (export them, or run a bounded parallel-redemption window with a manual liability list), card-on-file customers whose stored tokens usually cannot port between providers and must be re-captured, recurring appointment deposits; surfaces the old contract's known facts honestly - equipment-return obligations on leased terminals, notice windows, early-termination terms the merchant may have forgotten - without advising on their legal effect; and schedules the switch into the merchant's slowest trading window with the old system kept restorable until first settlement verifies.

included: honest surfacing of legacy contract obligations
excluded: legal advice on the old contract
negotiating the merchant's exit terms for them

pros.claim: A timed cutover with a restorable fallback removes the acceptance gap that costs a merchant their busiest day
pros.example: a diner switching Monday morning after Sunday's final legacy batch, with the old terminal boxed but connectable until Thursday's deposit lands

cons.claim: Parallel windows and staged switches add days of coordination the merchant experiences as slowness
cons.example: a salon owner impatient at running two systems for a week to bleed down gift-card redemptions

failure_modes: shutting the legacy system down with gift-card balances unexported and unredeemable
discovering the leased legacy terminal's return obligation after it was thrown away
acceptance_tests: the cutover runbook shows the batch/first-live timeline, the migration disposition of every crossing liability, the legacy obligations surfaced to the merchant in writing, and the restore-path expiry
revisit_triggers: the legacy provider changes export capability or return process
a crossing liability class appears that the runbook template does not cover

base.update_signal: legacy-provider export/return mechanics or crossing-liability classes change

nodes.definition: Configure the payment-behavior features that carry legal and network weight. Tips: choose capture mode by service environment - at-payment prompts for counter service, post-auth tip adjust for table service where the batch must reflect adjusted totals, pooled versus direct attribution per the owner's stated policy - and set prompt levels the owner chose, not defaults that embarrass their counter. Surcharging and cash discounting: treat them as regulated program classes, not toggles - permissibility, caps, registration duties and receipt-disclosure requirements differ by jurisdiction and card network and change over time, so the rule is verify current state law and network rules for this merchant before enabling anything, configure the disclosure exactly as the applicable rules require, and refuse copy-the-shop-next-door requests until verified. Misconfigured gratuity or an unlawful surcharge is a merchant-facing liability the agent installed.

included: tip capture mode per service model
excluded: wage-and-hour advice on tip pooling - flag to the owner's advisors

pros.claim: Environment-matched tip capture protects both the batch math and the staff's income from day one
pros.example: table-service tip adjust configured so servers add tips at close and the batch settles adjusted totals instead of stranding gratuities

cons.claim: The verification-first rule on surcharge programs delays a feature merchants demand loudly
cons.example: a mechanic pointing at the tire shop next door's card fee while the agent verifies the state's current rules

failure_modes: enabling a surcharge program in a jurisdiction or under network rules that forbid or cap it differently
counter-service tip prompts left at aggressive defaults the owner never chose
acceptance_tests: every enabled gratuity or price-signaling feature has a config record naming who verified the applicable rules, when, and the disclosure text configured
revisit_triggers: state law or a card network changes surcharge/cash-discount rules
the merchant changes service model or tip policy

base.update_signal: a jurisdiction or network rule change touching surcharge, discount or gratuity handling

nodes.definition: Give the payment stack its own clean lane on the merchant's network: a dedicated VLAN or at minimum a separate SSID for POS and terminals, guest Wi-Fi isolated so a customer's laptop can never see a payment device, factory default passwords eliminated on the router and every managed device, remote-access features disabled or locked to the platform's documented method, and firmware brought current at install. This is the practical half of PCI scope containment and also plain reliability engineering - a POS sharing an open network with the jukebox and the security DVR inherits every one of their failures. The survey found the topology; this node fixes it before the first live card is ever presented.

excluded: enterprise network engineering beyond the small-merchant class

pros.claim: Segmenting at install costs an hour; segmenting after a live incident costs the relationship
pros.example: the taqueria's guest Wi-Fi outage that no longer takes the ordering handhelds down with it

cons.claim: Consumer-grade gear at small merchants makes clean segmentation clumsy and sometimes requires new hardware the deal did not budget
cons.example: an ISP-issued combo router with no VLAN support forcing a small switch purchase

failure_modes: leaving terminals on the guest SSID because it was faster on install day
default admin credentials left on the router that fronts the payment lane
acceptance_tests: an install-day check confirms payment devices sit on their own segment, guest isolation holds under test, no default credentials remain, and firmware versions are recorded
revisit_triggers: the merchant swaps ISP or router hardware
a new connected device (cameras, music, kiosk) lands on the network

base.update_signal: network hardware changes at the site or a device inventory change

nodes.definition: Treat PCI-DSS scope as something the deployment design largely decides: a validated P2PE solution with encrypting readers keeps usable card data out of the merchant's POS, network and hands, which is the difference between a short attestation and a long one; segmentation keeps non-payment systems out of scope; and behavioral rules - no writing card numbers on order slips, no keying cards into anything but the terminal, no storing card data in the appointment book - keep the merchant from re-expanding scope by habit. The agent's role is scope-shrinking design plus orientation: explain what the merchant will attest, point them into the processor's compliance program, flag that SAQ classes and requirements are set by the current PCI-DSS version and the processor's program (verify, do not recite), and record that the attestation path was started. The agent is not a QSA and does not certify anyone.

included: merchant behavioral rules against scope creep
excluded: asserting SAQ types as fixed facts - version-specific, verify current

pros.claim: Scope decided at design time makes the merchant's annual attestation a form-filling exercise instead of a remediation project
pros.example: a salon on validated P2PE with a segmented network answering a short questionnaire instead of hiring help for a long one

cons.claim: Compliance framing at deployment can read as upsell theater to a merchant who has never been breached
cons.example: an owner waving off the no-card-numbers-on-tickets rule as big-company paranoia

failure_modes: deploying a stack that leaves the POS in the card-data path without telling the merchant what that means for their attestation
treating PCI as a leaflet in the box instead of a started path with a named program
acceptance_tests: the deployment record states the card-data path, the scope-relevant design choices, the behavioral rules delivered to staff, and the date the merchant was enrolled or oriented into the compliance program
revisit_triggers: a PCI-DSS version change or processor compliance-program change
the merchant adds a channel (online ordering, invoicing) that changes the card-data path

base.update_signal: PCI-DSS version, program requirements or the merchant's card-data path changes

nodes.definition: Execute the install as the survey scripted it: mount and cable stations, printers, drawers and kitchen devices along the planned paths; join every device to the segmented payment network; pair peripherals and verify kitchen routing prints where the profile said it should; load the frozen menu build; configure receipts, tips per the config decisions, and the batch/auto-close schedule; then run the test matrix before any customer is in front of the counter - sale, void, refund, partial payment, tip adjust where applicable, offline-mode capture and recovery, and a full end-of-day close that produces a batch. Install happens inside the surveyed quiet window, only after underwriting approval put a live merchant account behind the terminals, and it ends with the site physically tidy - cable chaos at the counter is what merchants photograph.

included: the pre-live test matrix including offline behavior
excluded: electrical or ISP work beyond the remediation list

pros.claim: A scripted test matrix catches configuration faults while they are free to fix
pros.example: the refund test exposing a mis-linked settlement account before a single customer transaction exists

cons.claim: Full-matrix discipline extends install day, and rushed crews are tempted to skip the closes and offline tests
cons.example: an installer skipping the end-of-day close test at a late-running install - exactly the step whose failure surfaces at that night's close

failure_modes: installing before approval and parking dead terminals in front of an angry owner
skipping the offline-mode test in a shop whose internet the survey already flagged as shaky
acceptance_tests: the signed install checklist shows every device on the payment segment, every test-matrix item passed with the batch produced, and the site photographed tidy
revisit_triggers: hardware or platform version changes alter the install or pairing procedure
a test-matrix gap is exposed by a post-live fault

base.update_signal: platform install procedures change or post-live faults trace to install steps

nodes.definition: Train by role, not by lecture: cashiers and servers drill the flows their shift actually contains - ringing with modifiers, splits and partial payments, tip capture, what the offline banner means and what to do when it appears; managers additionally drill voids versus refunds and when each is right, comps and discounts, drawer counts, the end-of-day close, and where the reports live; the owner sees user administration and permission levels so departed staff lose access the same day. Counter habits that later become chargeback and PCI problems are trained here as normal procedure - never write a card number down, never key a card the customer can dip themselves. Because these shops churn staff, the training must outlive the trainees: laminated quick-reference cards at the station, a short recorded walkthrough, and one designated in-house trainer taught to teach.

pros.claim: Role-based drills produce a floor that runs without the agent by the second day
pros.example: the closing manager running end-of-day alone on day two because she performed it three times supervised, not because she watched a demo

cons.claim: Training time competes with service hours and owners routinely under-schedule it
cons.example: a restaurant that books one hour before Friday dinner rush for the entire staff

failure_modes: training only the owner, who then becomes the single point of failure for every close
leaving no artifacts, so the third hiring wave learns folklore instead of procedure
acceptance_tests: each role demonstrates its core flows unaided, the quick-reference cards are physically at the stations, and a named in-house trainer has run one supervised teaching pass
revisit_triggers: staff turnover replaces the trained core
a software update changes the flows the cards and recording show

base.update_signal: turnover events or software-flow changes invalidate the trained material

nodes.definition: Run the first live days as a staffed hypercare window, not a goodbye: the agent or a competent tech is on-site for the first service rush, watches the first real orders move from counter to kitchen, fixes menu, routing and tax errors on the spot from a live punch list, walks the closing manager through the first true end-of-day close, and stays reachable on a direct line - not the platform's general queue - until the first settlement verifies. Hypercare also triages by escalation lane: agent-fixable configuration now, platform-vendor defects to the vendor with a ticket the agent owns, processor-side funding or hold questions to the processor with the agent conferenced in. The window closes on stability criteria, not on the calendar alone.

excluded: permanent free support - portfolio-phase support terms take over

pros.claim: On-site presence during the first rush converts day-one faults from trust-destroyers into trust-builders
pros.example: fixing the mis-routed appetizer printer between the first and second lunch tickets while the owner watches it get fixed

cons.claim: Hypercare is expensive attention that caps how many go-lives a week the operation can honestly run
cons.example: two same-week restaurant launches leaving one floor unwatched during its first Friday rush

failure_modes: leaving after installation and letting the merchant discover close procedures alone at midnight
absorbing every issue personally instead of opening the vendor and processor lanes with owned tickets
acceptance_tests: the hypercare log shows day-one attendance through the first rush, every punch-list item closed or ticketed with an owner, the supervised first close, and the stability criteria met before exit
revisit_triggers: post-handoff issue volume shows the window closed too early
a new product in the bundle changes what hypercare must watch

base.update_signal: post-handoff fault rates or bundle changes alter the hypercare checklist

nodes.definition: Prove the money path before calling anything done: after the first real batches close, trace each batch total to the deposit that lands in the merchant's account, confirm the funding timing matches what the merchant was told to expect, check the statement descriptor so the owner recognizes the deposit instead of fearing fraud, and reconcile expected deductions as mechanism (whether fees net from deposits daily or bill monthly changes what a correct deposit looks like - read the merchant's actual program setup rather than assuming). A missing or short first deposit has a short list of causes - miskeyed bank account at application, a risk hold from volume outrunning the boarded profile, tip-adjust variance between captured and settled totals, or normal timing the merchant misread - and each has a named fix path with the processor. Nothing builds or destroys a new merchant's confidence faster than the first deposit.

included: short-deposit cause diagnosis and processor fix path
excluded: explaining or optimizing the fee economics - residual-book territory

pros.claim: Verifying the first deposits catches boarding-configuration errors inside the first settlement cycle instead of at month-end
pros.example: a transposed account digit found Tuesday because the agent traced Monday's batch, recovered with one processor call instead of a month of misdirected funds

cons.claim: Deposit tracing needs the merchant's banking visibility, which some owners are slow to share
cons.example: waiting two days for a screenshot of the bank feed to confirm the first funding arrived

failure_modes: declaring success on approved transactions without ever confirming funds arrived
misreading gross-versus-net funding setup and alarming the merchant over a correct deposit
acceptance_tests: a reconciliation note maps each of the first batches to its landed deposit with dates, descriptor confirmed by the owner, and any variance explained and resolved with the processor
revisit_triggers: the funding model, batch schedule or bank account changes
a later hold or funding anomaly reopens the trace

base.update_signal: funding model, schedule or account changes for the merchant

nodes.definition: Write the deployment down while it happens so the merchant's future is serviceable by someone other than the installer's memory: equipment inventory with serials and ownership structure (sold, leased, placed), the network map with the payment segment and credentials held under the agent's credential policy, the menu build version and freeze-date change log, the configuration decisions (tips, taxes, batch schedule, any verified price-signaling program with its verification note), training artifacts and the named in-house trainer, the support contact tree across agent, platform and processor, and warranty and RMA paths per device. The record is the handoff artifact portfolio management inherits - without it every future support call re-derives the site from scratch and every equipment swap is archaeology.

included: equipment, network, configuration and training documentation
excluded: portfolio-phase account records - residuals, margin, support history

pros.claim: A live-written record makes every later support interaction start from facts instead of archaeology
pros.example: a year-later printer swap resolved remotely because the record named the model, port and routing assignment

cons.claim: Documentation discipline is the first casualty of a rushed install week and reconstructed records quietly lie
cons.example: a network map drawn from memory a month later showing a switch that was actually returned

failure_modes: credentials stored nowhere, or worse, on a sticky note on the router
the record written after the fact and wrong about what was actually configured
acceptance_tests: the record is completed during install and hypercare, covers equipment, network, configuration, training and support-tree sections, and a second person can locate every credential under the policy
revisit_triggers: any post-live change to equipment, network or configuration
a support call reveals the record disagrees with the site

base.update_signal: site changes or record-versus-site mismatches found in support

nodes.definition: Run the deployment calendar as a capacity-bounded pipeline rather than a pile of promises: equipment ordering and staging lead times tracked per platform, install dates held tentative until underwriting approval converts them to firm, per-vertical checklist templates so a salon deployment does not reinvent the restaurant's, buffer days between go-lives so hypercare never splits across two first-rushes, and a visible board of every merchant's stage (intake, underwriting, build, install, hypercare, handoff) so the next bottleneck is seen before it bites. The pipeline's honest constraint is hypercare capacity - the number of go-lives a week the operation can genuinely stand behind - and the discipline is refusing bookings past it even when the sales side is hot.

excluded: long-run support staffing economics - portfolio territory

pros.claim: A capacity-bounded calendar keeps every merchant's go-live properly attended instead of heroically half-attended
pros.example: moving a c-store install by four days so it does not share a week with two restaurant launches already booked

cons.claim: Capacity discipline delays revenue and frustrates the sales side when the pipeline is full
cons.example: a hot referral cooling while the calendar shows the next open go-live slot two weeks out

failure_modes: booking firm install dates on unapproved files and cancelling on merchants who scheduled staff
overbooking go-lives until hypercare becomes a phone number instead of a presence
acceptance_tests: the stage board shows every active merchant, no firm date precedes its approval, and no week carries more go-lives than the stated hypercare capacity
revisit_triggers: lead times shift on equipment or underwriting
hypercare capacity changes with staffing

base.update_signal: lead-time, approval-cycle or hypercare-capacity shifts

nodes.definition: Close the deployment through a gate, not a fade-out: the definition-of-done from the frame is checked item by item - live processing on the fitted stack, first settlement traced and reconciled, staff demonstrably self-sufficient with artifacts in place, the deployment record complete, the PCI attestation path started, the cutover's crossing liabilities fully landed - and whatever fails the check either gets fixed or transfers as a named open issue with an owner and a date, never silently. The merchant is told the transition explicitly: who they call now, what the support terms are, and that the relationship continues under account management. This gate is the boundary with the residual-book KB; a merchant handed off dirty comes back as churn attributed to deployment.

pros.claim: A checked gate makes deployment quality measurable and keeps early churn from being mislabeled as a retention problem
pros.example: the bounce-back log showing three handoffs failed on untrained closers - a training fix, not a retention fix

cons.claim: A strict gate can hold a functioning merchant in deployment limbo over a checklist item that does not threaten them
cons.example: a stable diner held for a delayed laminated card reprint

failure_modes: handing off with unlanded gift-card liability that detonates in month two
no explicit transition, so the merchant keeps calling the installer forever and the installer keeps answering
acceptance_tests: the signed gate record shows each done-definition item passed or transferred as a named open issue with owner and date, and the merchant's acknowledgment of the transition
revisit_triggers: bounce-backs from portfolio management within the early weeks
the done-definition changes upstream

base.update_signal: bounce-back patterns or a changed done-definition

edges.why_related: the conduct rules are written against the frame's scope - they govern exactly the steps deployment owns
intake is the first activity inside the frame's signed-agreement-to-live scope
profiling starts the solution-design lane the frame defines as deployment's core work
the no-coaching rule binds intake: application facts are the merchant's true facts, collected not composed
equipment commissions and lease incentives pull against right-sizing and plain disclosure
edges.resolution_rule: fit and disclosure win: the stack is sized by the workflow profile and no structure is signed without the plain-language total-obligation summary - walk away from the deal before violating either

edges.why_related: the stack decision is tested feature-by-feature against the profile's requirements sheet
the profile determines what data structure the build needs - coursing, providers, price book or job lines
classification and volume profiling draw on the intake packet's history and business facts
the packet is the file underwriting reads; its completeness sets the path's cycle time
the boarded classification and volume profile are core inputs the processor's review verifies
packet defects - mismatches, missing owners, absent proofs - cause the majority of stalls the triage playbook handles
triage responds to the path's stated pend and decline reasons stage by stage
install follows approval - terminals without a live merchant account behind them are furniture
the cutover date is committed only after approval makes the new processing path real
the chosen platform dictates the build's data model, import tools and modifier structure
the stack choice - validated P2PE or not - largely decides the merchant's card-data path and scope
the survey's topology findings define what segmentation work the site needs
the install executes the survey's script and depends on its remediation list being done
segmentation is the concrete network half of the scope-containment argument
install loads the frozen, owner-proofed build; installing an unproofed menu ships its errors live
the build's residual error rate is the main driver of hypercare's day-one punch-list volume
no live transaction runs on an unsegmented or default-credentialed network - the install waits for the lane to be clean
training runs on the installed, configured system so staff drill the real flows, not a demo
hypercare defends what install produced; its punch list starts from the install checklist's state
hypercare assumes a trained floor; untrained staff turn the window into remedial training
go-live executes the cutover's timeline - last legacy batch, first live transaction, restore-path custody
both translate the merchant's daily operation into the new system - one as data structure, one as human procedure - and defects in either present identically as day-one counter chaos
tip-adjust misconfiguration surfaces as variance between captured and settled totals in the first batches
the funding trace runs on the first real batches hypercare's closes produce
day-one punch-list corrections flow back into the build and its post-freeze change log
funding holds and anomalies loop back to boarded-profile facts that must be corrected with the processor
the record is written during install from what was actually mounted, cabled and configured
the done gate requires the traced, reconciled first settlement as its money-path proof
the record is the artifact the gate physically hands to portfolio management
booking more go-lives serves throughput while each go-live demands undivided hypercare attention
edges.resolution_rule: hypercare wins: no new go-live is booked into a week already at stated hypercare capacity, and a just-live merchant keeps their coverage through first verified settlement even if it idles the install crew

edges.why_related: the calendar wants firm dates while underwriting's clock is the processor's and can pend any file
edges.resolution_rule: approval gates the calendar: install and cutover dates stay tentative until the processor's approval exists, and merchants are told the date firms only at approval

edges.why_related: a full-replacement stack maximizes what must cross the cutover seam, while reprogramming minimizes the seam but may under-serve the workflow
edges.resolution_rule: the workflow profile decides: replace only what the profile shows the merchant needs replaced, and when replacement is right, the cutover plan absorbs the migration burden explicitly rather than discovering it live

edges.why_related: gate results and bounce-back patterns feed revisions of the done-definition and the deployment playbook

conflict_axes.name: activation_speed_vs_clean_file
conflict_axes.description: The agent is paid on activation and the merchant wants a launch date, but a rushed application with unverified facts pends longer than a clean one takes - and a shaded fact can kill the account later.
poles: submit fast and fix in flight
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: speed comes from checklist rigor before submission, never from shading facts; a pend costs more days than intake verification costs hours

conflict_axes.name: equipment_revenue_vs_merchant_fit
conflict_axes.description: Sale and lease structures pay the agent more when the stack is bigger, while the merchant's interest is the smallest stack that runs their day - the vertical's oldest conflict of interest.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: the profile's requirements sheet is the referee: every proposed component must map to a profiled need, and the structure's total obligation is disclosed in plain language before signature

conflict_axes.name: install_throughput_vs_hypercare_depth
conflict_axes.description: More go-lives per week grows the book faster, but each go-live needs on-site hypercare through first settlement, and split attention turns launches into churn seeds.
poles: book every install the crew can physically do
cap go-lives at real hypercare capacity
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: capacity is stated as go-lives per week the operation can attend properly; the calendar refuses past it and the buffer between launches is protected

conflict_axes.name: platform_standardization_vs_vertical_fit
conflict_axes.description: Standardizing on one POS platform compounds the agent's expertise, spare-parts bench and training materials, but no single platform is best for every vertical in the book.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: standardize per vertical, not per book: a small approved set - one restaurant platform, one retail/c-store platform, one services platform - keeps mastery compounding without forcing bad fits

conflict_axes.name: cutover_speed_vs_continuity
conflict_axes.description: The merchant and the agent both want the switch done, but compressing the cutover risks an acceptance gap, orphaned gift-card liability and a burned restore path.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: compress only what has no crossing liability; anything carrying balances, stored customers or return obligations gets a staged window and the old system stays restorable until first settlement verifies

conflict_axes.name: training_depth_vs_floor_hours
conflict_axes.description: Real competence needs supervised repetitions, but every training hour is an hour the owner is paying staff not to serve customers - so owners under-schedule exactly the practice that prevents day-one chaos.
poles: train until each role demonstrates unaided
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: split training across roles and shifts in short focused blocks, put artifacts at the stations, and make the unaided demonstration the exit test so depth is measured, not clocked

conflict_axes.name: pci_rigor_vs_small_merchant_friction
conflict_axes.description: Tight scope containment - P2PE, segmentation, behavioral rules - protects the merchant, but at a two-terminal shop the cost and ceremony can feel absurd and breed resistance.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: the non-negotiables are cheap and fixed (segmentation, no default credentials, no card data by hand); beyond them, scale ceremony to the merchant's actual card-data path rather than importing enterprise ritual

conflict_axes.name: feature_richness_vs_counter_speed
conflict_axes.description: Every configured feature - prompts, modifiers, loyalty asks, tip screens - adds seconds at the counter, and in a c-store or QSR the counter's speed is the business.
poles: configure only what the rush can afford
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: time the rush transaction path during the proof pass and strip any prompt whose value the owner cannot name; features can be added after live, but a slow counter poisons week one

conflict_axes.name: disclosure_completeness_vs_deal_momentum
conflict_axes.description: Reading out lease totals, cancellation terms and surcharge duties can stall a signature a competitor would just take, so momentum pressures the agent to summarize thinly.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: disclosure is non-negotiable and front-loaded: the plain-language summary travels with the proposal so the signing moment confirms what was already read, and a deal that dies of disclosure was a dispute prepaid

edge_cases.description: The approved application says the LLC but the bank letter carries the owner's personal name, and the first settlement is routed into a mismatch review
edge_cases.trigger: intake consistency check missed a name/banking mismatch
edge_cases.mitigation: run the written consistency check before submission; on a live mismatch, correct the banking record with the processor immediately and trace the held funds to release

edge_cases.description: A 30-percent owner lives abroad without the ID class the KYC check accepts, and the file stalls in beneficial-ownership review
edge_cases.trigger: ownership structure exceeds the KYC path's standard document set
edge_cases.mitigation: ask the processor for its documented alternative-verification options and collect them once; never restructure ownership on paper to dodge the check

edge_cases.description: Mid-underwriting, the principal's prior MATCH placement from a failed venture surfaces and the processor declines
edge_cases.trigger: MATCH screening hits on a disclosed-too-late history
edge_cases.mitigation: ask about processing history at intake so the placement is disclosed up front and routed to processors that handle that class; never re-mask the principal behind a fresh entity or nominee owner

edge_cases.description: The restaurant owner keeps changing prices and items daily while the menu build is underway, and the proof pass can never close
edge_cases.trigger: no menu freeze was declared before the build started
edge_cases.mitigation: declare the freeze date at build kickoff; changes after freeze queue into the post-live change log, and the proof pass runs against the frozen version

edge_cases.description: The site survey finds one ISP-issued router on factory credentials carrying the guest Wi-Fi, the security DVR and the proposed POS lane
edge_cases.trigger: small-merchant network topology cannot host a compliant payment lane as-is
edge_cases.mitigation: put segmentation hardware and credential resets on the remediation list as install gates; the first live card waits for the clean lane

edge_cases.description: The legacy terminal turns out to be leased with a return obligation and the old contract's termination terms were never read
edge_cases.trigger: cutover planning discovers unexamined legacy obligations
edge_cases.mitigation: surface the return duty and termination terms to the merchant in writing as facts to act on, timeline the return into the cutover, and route legal questions to the merchant's advisor

edge_cases.description: The salon's legacy gift-card balances cannot be exported and the old provider goes read-only at termination
edge_cases.trigger: crossing liability with no data path across the seam
edge_cases.mitigation: before termination, pull a manual balance list while access exists, run a bounded parallel-redemption window, and load or honor balances on the new stack from the list

edge_cases.description: The owner insists on going live Friday because staff are scheduled, and Friday is the shop's biggest day
edge_cases.trigger: go-live date set by staffing convenience instead of risk
edge_cases.mitigation: hold the rule that first live service runs in the slowest window with hypercare present; a Tuesday launch that wobbles is a story, a Friday launch that wobbles is a refund line

edge_cases.description: The first deposit never lands because one digit of the account number was transposed at boarding
edge_cases.trigger: banking data error invisible until funding
edge_cases.mitigation: trace the first batch to the first deposit within the expected funding window as standard practice; on a miss, open the correction with the processor same-day and track the misdirected funds to recovery

edge_cases.description: The merchant demands surcharging enabled at install because the shop next door charges a card fee
edge_cases.trigger: feature request whose legality is jurisdiction- and network-specific
edge_cases.mitigation: hold enablement until current state law and network rules are verified for this merchant, configure the required disclosures exactly, and document who verified what and when - the neighbor's setup is not a precedent

edge_cases.description: Two weeks after go-live the trained closing manager quits and nobody left on staff can run end-of-day
edge_cases.trigger: turnover erases the trained core before habits transfer
edge_cases.mitigation: train a second closer and a named in-house trainer before gate exit, leave station cards and the recorded walkthrough, and offer a paid refresher session as the defined re-training path

edge_cases.description: The c-store's lottery-season weekend triples volume over the boarded estimate and the processor freezes funding pending review
edge_cases.trigger: real volume outruns the honest but stale boarded profile
edge_cases.mitigation: profile known seasonal spikes into the application, and when growth is real, proactively re-profile with the processor before the spike rather than after the freeze - never split transactions to duck velocity checks

workflow.action: Frame the deployment scope and definition-of-done
workflow.description: Fix the signed-agreement-to-stabilized-live scope, the done checklist, and the borders with acquisition and portfolio work
workflow.gate: entry event, done items and both sibling-phase borders are stated in writing

workflow.action: Bind the engagement to disclosure-first conduct
workflow.description: Put the plain-language disclosure, no-coaching and verified-claims-only rules in force for this merchant
workflow.artifact: disclosure summary template and conduct checklist
workflow.gate: the equipment-structure summary format exists and the no-coaching rule is acknowledged by everyone touching the file

workflow.action: Assemble and consistency-check the intake packet
workflow.description: Collect entity, ownership, ID, banking and history documents and run the cross-document consistency check
workflow.gate: the written consistency check passes with no name, address, ownership or banking mismatch

workflow.action: Profile the vertical and select the stack
workflow.description: Write the workflow profile from observation and interview, then map it to reprogram/smart-terminal/full-POS and an honestly structured acquisition
workflow.gate: every profiled non-negotiable maps to a demonstrated feature and the structure's total obligation is in the merchant's summary

workflow.action: Classify honestly and submit to underwriting
workflow.description: Set truthful MCC, volume and mix, submit the clean file, and shepherd information requests same-day
workflow.gate: approval (or conditioned approval) received and logged; declines routed per the triage playbook

workflow.action: Survey the site and clear remediations
workflow.description: Audit network, power, space, signal and busy hours; assign every remediation an owner and a due date
workflow.artifact: site survey record with remediation list
workflow.gate: all install-gating remediations closed before the install date

workflow.description: Build the dedicated payment segment, isolate guest traffic, kill default credentials, update firmware
workflow.artifact: network map with segment and credential record
workflow.gate: isolation holds under test and no default credential remains on the payment path

workflow.action: Build, tax-map and proof the menu or catalog
workflow.description: Construct items, modifiers and routing per the profile, verify tax categories locally, freeze, and run the owner proof pass
workflow.gate: proof pass signed against realistic rung orders with tax lines verified

workflow.description: Time last-batch to first-live, disposition every crossing liability, surface legacy obligations in writing
workflow.gate: no acceptance gap in the timeline, every crossing liability has a disposition, restore path defined with expiry

workflow.description: Execute the surveyed install in the quiet window, load the frozen build, run the full test matrix including offline and close
workflow.artifact: signed install checklist with test log
workflow.gate: every test-matrix item passes, a batch was produced, and all devices sit on the payment segment

workflow.action: Train staff by role and leave artifacts
workflow.description: Drill cashier/server, manager and owner flows on the live system; place cards, recording and the in-house trainer
workflow.artifact: training log, station cards, trainer designation
workflow.gate: each role demonstrates its flows unaided and artifacts are physically in place

workflow.action: Run hypercare, verify settlement, and gate the handoff
workflow.description: Attend the first rush, fix the punch list, trace first batches to deposits, then check the done-definition item by item and transfer with named open issues
workflow.artifact: hypercare log, settlement reconciliation, signed handoff gate record
workflow.gate: first settlement reconciled, done items passed or transferred with owner and date, merchant acknowledges the transition

dominance_rules.rule: Underwriting approval dominates the install calendar
dominance_rules.rationale: installed terminals without an approved merchant account are dead weight and broken promises
dominance_rules.trigger: pressure to fix an install or cutover date before the processor's verdict exists
dominance_rules.action: keep the date tentative, tell the merchant it firms at approval, and never stage equipment on an unapproved file

dominance_rules.rule: Honest application facts dominate activation speed
dominance_rules.rationale: a shaded MCC, volume or ownership fact is a misrepresentation that surfaces as holds, termination or MATCH placement
dominance_rules.trigger: any temptation or request to adjust facts to ease approval
dominance_rules.action: submit the merchant's true facts with evidence, and walk away from a deal that needs a lie to board

dominance_rules.rule: The processor's verdict dominates the agent's forecast
dominance_rules.rationale: underwriting decisions belong to the processor; the agent who promises approval owns a promise they cannot keep
dominance_rules.trigger: a merchant asks for certainty on approval or timing
dominance_rules.action: state what was submitted and the process, commit only to same-day responses on information requests

dominance_rules.rationale: a mis-fitted stack churns the account, and the churned account outweighs any equipment margin
dominance_rules.trigger: a bigger sale or lease beckons beyond what the profile supports
dominance_rules.action: size to the requirements sheet and let the plain-language summary carry the structure chosen

dominance_rules.rationale: a gap in card acceptance costs the merchant real revenue and the relationship its credibility
dominance_rules.trigger: pressure to compress the cutover past its liability dispositions
dominance_rules.action: hold the staged timeline and the restore path until first settlement verifies

dominance_rules.rule: Verified rules dominate any surcharge or cash-discount request
dominance_rules.rationale: price-signaling programs are governed by changing state law and network rules; the neighbor's config proves nothing
dominance_rules.trigger: a request to enable surcharging, cash discounting or a copied fee scheme
dominance_rules.action: verify the current rules for this merchant's jurisdiction and networks, configure disclosures exactly, and document the verification - or refuse

dominance_rules.rationale: an unattended first rush converts config noise into churn and reputation damage that no extra install offsets
dominance_rules.trigger: the calendar wants a go-live in a week already at hypercare capacity
dominance_rules.action: move the new booking, never the coverage of the merchant already going live

dominance_rules.rationale: a POS on the guest network with default credentials is a breach and a scope explosion waiting on a bored teenager
dominance_rules.trigger: install-day temptation to ship on the existing flat network and fix it later
dominance_rules.action: the first live card waits for segmentation, credential resets and current firmware - no exceptions

dominance_rules.rationale: an undisclosed lease term or fee program becomes a dispute with the agent's name on it
dominance_rules.trigger: a signing moment where the full summary has not been walked through
dominance_rules.action: stop and walk the summary; a lost deal costs less than an earned dispute

dominance_rules.rationale: approved transactions are not money; the deployment is proven when deposits land and reconcile
dominance_rules.trigger: pressure to close the engagement once the counter is ringing
dominance_rules.action: hold the gate until first batches trace to deposits and variances are resolved with the processor

anti_rework_rules.rule: Run the cross-document consistency check before submitting the application
anti_rework_rules.prevents: multi-day underwriting pends and post-live funding mismatches that each cost more than the check

anti_rework_rules.rule: Complete the site survey before ordering hardware
anti_rework_rules.prevents: wrong peripherals, unsupported topology and an install day spent shopping instead of installing

anti_rework_rules.rule: Declare the menu freeze before the build starts
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an endlessly reopened build whose proof pass can never close

anti_rework_rules.rule: Confirm underwriting approval before firming install and cutover dates
anti_rework_rules.prevents: cancelled installs, staged equipment on dead files, and merchants who scheduled staff for nothing

anti_rework_rules.rule: Segment the network and reset credentials before the first live transaction
anti_rework_rules.prevents: post-live re-cabling, scope explosion and the impossible conversation after an incident

anti_rework_rules.rule: Export gift-card balances and inventory crossing liabilities before terminating the legacy provider
anti_rework_rules.prevents: unrecoverable liability data behind a read-only or closed legacy account

anti_rework_rules.rule: Run the full test matrix including offline mode and end-of-day close before go-live
anti_rework_rules.prevents: first-night close failures and offline surprises in exactly the shops whose internet was already flagged

anti_rework_rules.rule: Train the managers and a second closer before the cashier wave
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a floor whose every question lands on an untrained manager and a close that dies with one resignation

anti_rework_rules.rule: Write the deployment record during install and hypercare, not after
anti_rework_rules.prevents: reconstructed documentation that disagrees with the site and misleads every future support call

iteration_protocol.trigger: an application pends or declines with a stated reason
iteration_protocol.action: repair per the triage playbook, resubmit or route honestly, and log the reason into the intake checklist loop

iteration_protocol.trigger: day-one order, tax or routing errors spike on the punch list
iteration_protocol.action: hotfix the catalog live, log changes in the post-freeze change log, and re-proof the affected sections with the owner

iteration_protocol.trigger: the first deposit is missing, short or unrecognized
iteration_protocol.action: trace batch to deposit, diagnose against the cause list, and open the correction with the processor same-day

iteration_protocol.trigger: real volume or mix diverges from the boarded profile
iteration_protocol.action: re-profile honestly with the processor before the next spike; never adapt by splitting transactions

iteration_protocol.trigger: turnover or a software update erodes staff competence
iteration_protocol.action: rerun role training through the in-house trainer with refreshed cards and recording

iteration_protocol.trigger: a PCI-DSS version, network rule or surcharge-law change lands
iteration_protocol.action: re-verify affected configurations and templates across the active book and update the deployment playbook

iteration_protocol.trigger: the same install-day surprise recurs across deployments
iteration_protocol.action: add the missing check to the survey template and the affected checklist items to the pipeline's templates

iteration_protocol.trigger: portfolio management bounces a handoff back within the early weeks
iteration_protocol.action: reopen hypercare for the merchant, fix the gap, and amend the done-definition so the gate catches it next time

priority_rationale: The frame and conduct rules come first because every later step inherits their scope and honesty constraints; intake, classification and underwriting must precede any physical commitment because the processor's approval gates the calendar; profile-driven selection, survey, segmentation and the menu build feed a single scripted install; training, cutover and hypercare convert the install into a running operation; and settlement verification, the deployment record and the done gate close the loop because a deployment is finished when money lands, knowledge is written down and portfolio management accepts a clean merchant.
